published_prior_art.cite: ChenDarwiche2024 gives functional elimination, not the exact-support completion iff.
Chen and Darwiche, Constrained Identifiability of Causal Effects (arXiv:2412.02869v2), gives AC-based constrained-ID examples but not a complete exact-support formula-or-rational-witness trichotomy.
Its substantive content is conditional on Open-ended Question 1 and is the advertised FID-S output packaging.

novelty_flags.label: Open-ended Question 1 / related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: The closest public comparator is omitted: Chen and Darwiche, arXiv:2412.02869v2, studies constrained identifiability with logical/0–1 constraints and AC invariant cuts; distinguish its non-complete method from the proposed trichotomy.

soundness_flags.label: Open-ended Question 1 and def:fids-handle
soundness_flags.one_line: “Preserving the original product law over U” is undefined because no latent-root law is an input: specify whether witnesses must share root masses or only retain the original source set and factorization.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 2 (thm:fids-trichotomy)
soundness_flags.one_line: Conditional on an affirmative Open-ended Question 1, the theorem merely restates the handle’s promised trichotomy, bounds, and formula reconstruction; add an independent compiler/certificate-verifier result or absorb it into the OEQ.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 15 eliminates observed functional non-treatment/non-outcome variables with observed parents that are separable from the positivity constraints; Theorem 18 assumes positivity for every treatment assignment and reduces F-identifiability to identifiability after adding reachable functional variables.
The paper adds positivity of the observational distribution to g-identifiability and supplies a sound-and-complete gID algorithm under that assumption.
The paper gives complete identification methods and an ID algorithm returning an expression or a hedge-bearing failure in the classical graphical setting.

The paper formalizes arbitrary model constraints, presents AC-based constrained-identifiability tests, and shows examples where zero entries or fixed observational distributions enable identification, while claiming completeness only relative to classical strict-positivity methods.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Chen–Darwiche’s constrained-identifiability preprint to related work and state a precise separation: AC invariant cuts are not complete over support-literal/functional classes and do not yield exact-support rational countermodels.

Replace “original product law over U” with a defined witness invariant, preferably preservation of the original root set and sourcewise factorization; if identical root marginals are intended, make that an explicit strengthened target.

Make Theorem 2 independent by proving a verifier/compiler theorem from a finite grammar certificate to a checked guarded formula or paired-model certificate, with its own state-to-bit-complexity accounting.

recommended_next_step: Revise the kernel’s witness invariant and derivative trichotomy theorem, then rerun novelty review with the omitted constrained-identifiability comparator integrated.
